title: Gujarat Has Launched Its Industrial Policy 2026. It Wants Semiconductor Factories, Ultra Mega Projects, and NRI Capital.
excerpt: The state expands its priority sectors from nine to sixteen, creates a new category for ₹10,000 crore investments, and puts green manufacturing at the centre of its pitch.
body:
Gujarat unveiled its Industrial Policy 2026 on Monday at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar, laying out an ambitious five-year framework that expands the state's roster of priority sectors from nine to sixteen and introduces a new "ultra mega" category for projects investing at least ₹10,000 crore and creating 3,000 or more jobs.

Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel and Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, who holds the industries portfolio, launched the policy at a ceremony attended by senior bureaucrats, representatives from the Confederation of Indian Industry's Gujarat chapter, and corporate stakeholders. Industry bodies praised the inclusion of green energy transition incentives and dedicated support for MSMEs — segments they said had been underserved in previous policy cycles.

Sixteen Thrust Sectors: From Semiconductors to Drones

The centrepiece of the new framework is the expansion of Gujarat's "thrust sectors" — priority industries that receive targeted incentives, land access, and infrastructure support. The seven new entrants include ancillary units for semiconductor manufacturing, nuclear power equipment, drone and robotics production, textile waste recycling, heavy equipment manufacturing, and advanced materials.

The additions track closely with national policy priorities. India's semiconductor mission has drawn global attention, with Gujarat's Dholera Special Investment Region already shortlisted for multiple chip fabrication projects. Nuclear power equipment gets a boost just days after the central government retrospectively waived customs duties on nuclear imports dating back to 2019.

**"## The Diaspora Angle

Gujarat has long been one of India's most NRI-connected states, with a global diaspora estimated at over 10 million."**

Units in the ultra mega category can receive incentives worth up to 40 per cent of their capital investment through a combination of capital subsidies, interest subsidies, and power tariff support — a scale of state backing that puts Gujarat in direct competition with Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and Telangana for anchor investments.

Project THRIVE: Moving Factories Out of Cities

The policy introduces Project THRIVE — Transition for Harmonized Relocation and Inclusive Vibrant Economy — an initiative to relocate industrial operations from within municipal corporation limits to new sites outside urban centres. The scheme offers financial incentives and expedited approvals for firms willing to move, a response to growing public pressure around urban pollution, congestion, and land-use conflicts in cities like Ahmedabad, Surat, and Vadodara.

For NRIs with family or business roots in Gujarat's cities, the relocation programme could reshape property dynamics — freeing up industrial land in urban areas while creating new industrial corridors with attendant infrastructure and housing development.

Sustainable Manufacturing and MSME Focus

!Mahatma Mandir — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The policy dedicates significant space to sustainable manufacturing, with incentives for green energy adoption, waste recycling, and circular economy practices. Officials confirmed that a streamlined single-window clearance system would be introduced, along with a new tier of incentives for units establishing operations in aspirational districts and tribal belt areas — an explicit attempt to reduce regional economic disparity within the state.

For the MSME sector, the framework introduces dedicated provisions for food processing, textiles, and handicrafts — industries with significant employment and cultural weight. Handloom and artisan clusters in Kutch and Surat are expected to benefit from new branding and export facilitation schemes embedded in the policy.

The Diaspora Angle

Gujarat has long been one of India's most NRI-connected states, with a global diaspora estimated at over 10 million. The industrial policy matters to this community not as an abstract governance document but as a signal of where the state's economic centre of gravity is shifting.

The semiconductor and drone manufacturing push could create new investment opportunities for diaspora-backed ventures. The green manufacturing incentives align with ESG mandates that increasingly govern NRI investment decisions. And the GIFT City connection — Hexaware Technologies just opened a delivery centre in the financial hub — positions Gujarat as a node for both manufacturing and high-end services.

The state attracted ₹13,070 crore in investment commitments at Davos in January. The Industrial Policy 2026 is the governance framework that will determine whether those commitments translate into factories, jobs, and returns.
